author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire Democrats moved quickly from intraparty competition to the general election Wednesday morning, gathering at Saint Anselm College for a kickoff breakfast one day after the state primary.

Party leaders and nominees used the event at the New Hampshire Institute of Politics to urge supporters of losing candidates to unite behind the full Democratic ticket. The message followed months of contested races, including a close 1st Congressional District primary won by Stefany Shaheen and the U.S. Senate primary won by Chris Pappas.

State party chair Ray Buckley said Democratic primary participation exceeded expectations and that more Democratic than Republican ballots were cast in a New Hampshire state primary for the first time since 2018. Manchester Ink Link reported that the program also emphasized protecting Social Security and other programs Democrats say Republicans may target.

Gubernatorial nominee Cinde Warmington drew on her own experience from a difficult 2024 primary while encouraging the party to bring rival campaigns back together. Shaheen and Pappas also recognized their former opponents. The nominees now have less than eight weeks to organize for the November 3 general election.
dek: Party leaders and nominees opened the general-election campaign with a unity event one day after New Hampshire’s state primary.
headline: New Hampshire Democrats turn to unity after state primary
